summary.text: Darline Graham is the Republican U.S. Senator from South Carolina, appointed by Gov. Henry McMaster on July 13, 2026 after the death of her brother, Lindsey Graham. Before the Senate she worked in state vocational-rehabilitation and disability-services agencies, and from 2019 headed the South Carolina Commission for the Blind. She won the Republican special primary runoff on August 25, 2026 and is running to complete the term.

paragraphs.text: Born in Central, South Carolina, on June 12, 1964. Her parents operated a restaurant and bar; her mother died when she was 11 and her father about 15 months later, after which she lived with an aunt and uncle in Seneca, with her brother Lindsey as her legal guardian.

Earned a bachelor's degree in sociology from the College of Charleston (1989) and a master's degree in rehabilitation counseling from South Carolina State University (2009); she is also a Certified Public Manager.

In 2008 she joined the South Carolina Vocational Rehabilitation Department, where she helped coordinate a remote-work program for adults with severe disabilities and by 2015 was public information director.

In 2019 she became commissioner and agency head of the South Carolina Commission for the Blind, which administers vocational rehabilitation, independent living and blindness-prevention programs. She also served on the South Carolina State Workforce Development Board and was elected president of the National Council of State Agencies for the Blind, with a term set to begin in January 2027.

Before her appointment she had not held elected office; she appeared in a 2002 television ad for her brother's Senate campaign and took part in his later campaigns, including introducing him at his 2016 presidential campaign launch.

Gov. Henry McMaster appointed her on July 13, 2026 to fill the vacancy created by Lindsey Graham's death, and she was sworn in July 14. She is the first woman to represent South Carolina in the U.S. Senate and the first senator to succeed a sibling.

In the 2026 special Republican primary on August 11 she placed first with 32.8% and advanced to a runoff against Rep. Ralph Norman, which she won on August 25 with 52.6% of the vote (180,231 to 162,497 per Ballotpedia).

Her committee assignments, per Wikipedia, are Appropriations, Budget, Environment and Public Works, and Judiciary. On July 16, 2026 she introduced the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, which passed both chambers and was signed into law in September.
Lives in Lexington, South Carolina, and has two daughters, according to Wikipedia.
